item.title: Report: Chinese President to visit Egypt for first time in a decade
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to visit Egypt next week, marking his first trip to the country in a decade, Al-Monitor reported.
According to China’s Foreign Ministry, the visit will be part of Xi’s diplomatic tour from August 30 to September 3, which will also include a visit to Kyrgyzstan and participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit. In Egypt, Xi is expected to meet with President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi.

item.title: Trump says he is 'not in a hurry' to resume Iran talks
item.description: Trump says he has no timetable for the Iran war and is “not in a hurry" to resume talks, while warning Tehran faces mounting economic pressure.

item.title: Qatar’s Prime Minister to travel to Tehran in bid to de-escalate tensions
item.description:
Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Majed Al Ansari, announced that Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed Al Thani will travel to Tehran on Thursday and meet with several senior officials.
He said the talks will focus on reducing tensions, “based on Qatar’s view that diplomacy is the right way to resolve conflicts."

item.title: US designates Palestine Action a 'transnational terror group'
item.description: The US Treasury designates UK-based Palestine Action a terrorist group, freezing its assets and barring US citizens and companies from doing business with it.

item.title: Explosions heard near Lebanon border amid IDF activity
item.description: Explosions were heard in communities near the Lebanon border amid IDF activity in the area.

item.title: FDA approves new pancreatic cancer drug after trial doubles patient survival
item.description: The FDA approves Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer after a trial showed the drug doubled survival for patients.

item.title: Shooting in Haifa: 70-year-old man seriously injured
item.description:
A man in his 70s was seriously injured in a shooting in Haifa and was evacuated to Rambam Hospital.
Carmel District police officers launched an investigation, collected evidence at the scene, and began searching for suspects. Police believe the shooting was criminally motivated.

item.title: The Lone Wolf Is not alone: What drives the stabbing Jihad
item.description: The decisive question is why one society’s political, religious and media institutions repeatedly provide a ready-made target, a heroic script and communal validation for those who commit terror. Op-ed.
